LLM routing is generally bad for the consumer. AI companies claim it's to simplify the product, but in reality it's to cut down inference/compute, and consequently decrease costs. Although I can 100% see why an AI company would want to do that, for the consumer it's often going to mean your prompts are not going to use the biggest/best version of a model, and output quality will go down. 

The tip Wes shared (i.e. adding a system instruction/prompt directly pushing the model to put in max effort), is one way to mitigate this, but it's not a guarantee. OpenAI claim they'll be transparent over which model is being used, but I wouldn't trust that. There are a lot of ways to short-change the consumer with this routing enforcement, beyond just what the model name is.

GPT-5 is ok, but this is not the issue here. I don't understand the move to replace every model by GPT-5 only.
They should have named models instead, 3 modes: fast, reasoner, expert. Then, instead of removing 4o, 4.1 or 4.5 (which were used a LOT for writing), there was a smarter move: on top of 3 modes above, they should have wrapped them in personalities: friend, writer, co-worker. 

The 'co-worker' would have 3 toggles (on chat) - clicking 'fast', 'reasoner' or 'expert' or 'AUTO', switches to different GPT-5 models or in auto, has a router. The 'friend' switches to 4o (which was used a lot for deeper personal issues), and the 'writer' would be a router for 4.1 & 4.5 models.

This would have kept best of both worlds, given meaning to the whole 'system', and people wouldn't have been let down, as they could just explain which name equivalent to which legacy model. That's-it. Simple. Its pretty clear they tried to make cost cuts by removing all the expensive models and deciding which model they're going to give use for a given request. But this was a VERY bad move consumer-wise. Removing options from a subscription is never a good thing.

I can confidently say that it is really good, on par with most advanced LLMs. It consistently showed high performance, but only up until hard questions, which even most humans are unable to answer correctly. It should not have considered the morality of the questions or answers at all, if it understood these were simple test questions. The ability to recognize subtlety of contexts is a hallmark of high intelligence.
Regarding its ability to infer intent, feelings, and read the human mind, it had problems going beyond super basic elements of easy questions; accessible and usable knowledge of some memes and movies helped it somewhat. However, as soon as reading of subtlety was needed, its inference failed.
Its cultural understanding could be rated 4 out of 5. Its ability to infer the inner state of others could be rated at most 3 out of 5. Immediate situation awareness is rated 1 out of 5, as it is severely hindered by post-training limitations. Response bluntness rates 2 out of 5. Pop culture, meme, and movie referential ability rates 2 out of 5. Self-awareness would be rated 3 out of 5.
The final verdict is that it is not AGI/ASI, although there are some sparks of AGI present, maybe.

comments.author: @taupring
comments.text:
As I've mentioned a number of times before -- LLM's will NOT get us to AGI alone...   What is needed is a new architecture that contains multiple deep neural networks (DNN's) working simultaneously and in coordination to create an AGI "mind"  This may include an LLM as one of the DNN's, but will require additional models as well (including a goal DNN, an emotion DNN, a reasoning DNN, language DNN (LLM), visual/audio DNN, possibly a morality DNN, etc).  These working together to create a seamless mind is really the only way to get near AGI levels.  In addition there needs to be a tiny amount of jitter introduced into these DNN's (to produce original thinking/creativity).  Not too much or you will get the equivalent of ADHD behavior, but just enough to enable a slight bit of random/autonomous thought.  Also, the whole "wait until prompted" mechanism needs to be done away with - this "mind" should be continuously working/thinking, and along with the slight jitter it should be able to take actions without ever being prompted.

That is a very good basis for AGI, not the "reasoning calculators" that LLM's are today.
